title: Projective Functors and the Soergel Functor in Category O

items.title: The coinvariant algebra of a finite Weyl group
items.statement: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ and Weyl group $W$ acting on $\mathfrak h$ by reflections, hence on the symmetric algebra $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ by graded algebra automorphisms. Write $S^W_+$ for the ideal of positive-degree invariants and $I:=S\,S^W_+$ for the ideal of $S$ it generates, so that $I$ is the specialization to the Weyl group of the homogeneous ideal of [[def-finite-linear-invariant-and-coinvariant-polynomial-algebras]]. The **coinvariant algebra** is $$C=C(\mathfrak h,W):=S/I.$$ It is a commutative graded $\mathbb C$-algebra with $C_0=\mathbb C$, a canonical surjection $\rho:S\to C$, and an induced action of $W$ by graded algebra automorphisms; $C$ is finite dimensional because $W$ is generated by reflections. The page fixes the degree normalization $\deg\mathfrak h=2$ used throughout the type-A Soergel material, so that the auxiliary permutation-coordinate model is $S_{\mathrm{perm}}=\mathbb k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ with the place-permuting $S_n$-action and $C\cong\mathbb k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(e_1,\dots,e_n)$ for the elementary symmetric polynomials $e_1,\dots,e_n$. Elements of $C$ are written as classes $\rho(f)$; no choice principle is used.
items.strategy: The published definition is quoted for a finite linear group and specialized to the reflection group case; the quotient by the ideal generated by positive-degree invariants is the same construction because $S^W_+$ is the space of invariants of positive degree. Degree normalization is a convention fixed here once for the whole page; For sl_n, split the permutation representation into its sum-zero Cartan and its fixed average coordinate. The fixed coordinate is the invariant e_1/n and is killed in the coinvariant quotient; therefore the auxiliary n-variable quotient by e_1,...,e_n is the Cartan coinvariant algebra, although the unreduced permutation polynomial ring has one extra variable. Products of factors use the corresponding tensor product.

items.title: The regular integral block and its antidominant weight
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory. Work in category $\mathcal O$ of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ with the conventions of [[def-bgg-category-o]]: Cartan $\mathfrak h$, positive system with simple roots $\alpha_i$, Weyl group $W$, Weyl vector $ho$ and dot action $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+ho)-ho$. Fix the **dominant regular integral representative** $\lambda$ of the block, i.e. $\langle\lambda+ho,\alpha^\veeangle
otin\{0\}$ for every root $\alpha$ and $\lambda$ integral in the sense of [[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]]; then the integral Weyl group of $\lambda$ is all of $W$, and the linkage class $C=W\cdot\lambda$ has exactly $|W|$ elements. Write $\mathcal O_\lambda:=\mathcal O_C$ for the corresponding block of [[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]]; it is a highest-weight category whose simple objects $L(w\cdot\lambda)$, standard objects $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)=M(w\cdot\lambda)$, costandard objects $
abla(w\cdot\lambda)$ and projective covers $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ are indexed by $w\in W$, with $\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ the unique simple standard object and the published triangularity $[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]=1$ and $[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(v\cdot\lambda)]
eq0\Rightarrow v\cdot\lambda\le w\cdot\lambda$ in the dominance order on the dot orbit ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[cor-projective-standard-labels-lie-above-the-head]]). The **antidominant** weight in the block is $w_0\cdot\lambda$, where $w_0$ is the longest element; $P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ is the antidominant projective. The Grothendieck group $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$ has the classes of the standards and of the simples as bases, as on [[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]].
items.strategy: The block decomposition, linkage classes and the description of central characters are the published items; integrality identifies the integral Weyl group with $W$ and hence the linkage class with the $|W|$-element dot orbit; regularity of $\lambda$ makes its dot-action stabilizer trivial used by the published translation-functor definitions. Indexing of simples and Vermas, the triangularity of the Verma-flag matrix ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]] with [[cor-projective-standard-labels-lie-above-the-head]], read in the direction $[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(v\cdot\lambda)]\neq0\Rightarrow v\cdot\lambda\le w\cdot\lambda$) and the Grothendieck-group bases are the published facts. Every regular integral block has a unique dominant representative in its dot orbit, and that representative is used throughout.

items.title: The sum of basic Weyl invariant degrees minus one counts positive roots
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from invariant theory. For a finite Weyl reflection group on its rank-r Cartan and basic invariant polynomial degrees d_1,...,d_r (ordinary degree one for Cartan generators), $$\sum_i(d_i-1)=|\Phi^+|.$$ With page degree two, the coinvariant top degree is twice this number.
items.strategy: Use the Molien trace identity, proved by averaging each finite symmetric power: product_i(1-t^{d_i})^{-1}=|W|^{-1}sum_w det(1-tw)^{-1}. Put u=1-t. The invariant Hilbert product is (product_i d_i)^{-1}u^{-r}[1+(sum_i(d_i-1)/2)u+O(u^2)]. The identity term on the right is |W|^{-1}u^{-r}; the terms with codimension-one fixed space each have eigenvalue -1 on its orthogonal complement, hence contribute (2|W|)^{-1}u^{-(r-1)}+O(u^{-(r-2)}). Every other term is lower order. A codimension-one fixed-space element is a root reflection: its fixed hyperplane cannot contain a root-regular point, since chamber stabilizers are trivial; hence that hyperplane is one of the finitely many root hyperplanes. There is one reflection for each positive root. The known product_i d_i=|W| and comparison of the next Laurent coefficient prove the formula. Rank zero gives empty sums; rank one has just identity/reflection and the same expansion. No degree table or unproved exponent identity is used.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Representations of Lie Groups, MIT18.757 full lecture notes (2023)
references.locator: Section 17.4, Exercise 17.5(i): the ordinary-degree identity; expanded here by the next Laurent coefficient of the Molien trace formula, using the published coinvariant Hilbert computation

items.title: Adjoint isotypic modules have the zero-weight rank
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For complex semisimple g and any finite-dimensional g-module E, the modules Hom_g(E,S(g)) over S(g)^g and Hom_g(E,U(g)) over Z(U(g)) are free of rank dim E_0. Under a g-equivariant harmonic decomposition S(g)=S(g)^g tensor H and its filtered PBW lift U(g)=Z tensor H, every central reduction has adjoint E-multiplicity dim E_0, compatibly with the natural quotient map.
items.strategy: It suffices to treat simple E and then direct sums. The harmonic decomposition and complete reducibility in each finite polynomial degree make Hom_g(E,Sg) a graded direct summand of a graded free invariant-ring module. A graded projective module bounded below with finite-dimensional graded pieces is graded free: choose homogeneous lifts of a basis modulo the positive invariant ideal, generate recursively by degree, split the resulting graded free surjection and use graded Nakayama on its kernel. Its basis multiplicity series H_E(q) has nonnegative coefficients, a priori possibly infinitely many. Character decomposition of Sym g and the polynomial invariant Hilbert series give sum_E H_E(q)chi_E=product_i[d_i]_q/product_{alpha in Phi}(1-q e^alpha). The Weyl character formula shows simple characters are orthonormal for the constant-term form (1/|W|)CT(phi psi* product_alpha(1-e^alpha)): substitute the alternating Weyl numerators; distinct dominant shifted orbits have zero constant cross term and each equal orbit has |W| terms. Hence H_E(q)=(product_i[d_i]_q/|W|)CT(chi_E* product_alpha(1-e^alpha)/(1-q e^alpha)). To justify the limit without an imported Haar argument, work on l2 of the full weight lattice, with shifts by roots. For a positive root alpha let U_alpha be the unitary shift and F_alpha(q)=(I-U_alpha)(I-qU_alpha)^{-1}. The norm-convergent geometric resolvent gives norm F_alpha<=2 and norm squared (F_alpha-I)delta_0=(1-q)/(1+q). The finitely many operators commute, so telescoping their product, moving the error factor to delta_0, proves F(q)delta_0->delta_0. For 0<=q<1 the constant term above is the inner product of this vector with its image under the finite Laurent-character shift operator; the negative-root factors are the adjoint positive-root factors. Geometric convergence and Cauchy-Schwarz justify the coefficient products. It tends to CT(chi_E*)=dim E_0. The prefactor tends to1 because product d_i=|W|. Nonnegative coefficients and this finite limit show the total number of homogeneous free generators is dim E_0, hence finite. Finally PBW symmetrization is g-equivariant; lifting the harmonic basis and the basic central symbols yields the filtered isomorphism Z tensor H->U by its associated graded isomorphism. Taking E-isotypics and then any central fiber proves the U and reduction assertions. This is the exact isotypic multiplicity statement, stronger than module freeness alone.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Representations of Lie Groups, MIT18.757 full lecture notes (2023)
references.locator: Section 13.1, Theorem 13.1 and its complete proof (printed pp. 71-73), and Section 13.5, Theorem 13.5 (printed p. 74): the isomorphism S(g) = S(g)^g tensor H and the isotypic multiplicity dim E_0 for the adjoint action, with the torus-limit replaced locally by the explicit finite root-lattice shift coefficient argument

items.title: Projective functors on a regular integral block
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory. For a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module $E$ and a block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ as in [[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]], let $\operatorname{pr}_\lambda:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_\lambda$ be the exact block projection of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]] and let $$F_E:=\operatorname{pr}_\lambda\circ(E\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_\lambda:\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow\mathcal O_\lambda .$$ By [[prop-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-category-o]] and [[lem-block-projection-preserves-projectives]] the functor $F_E$ is exact, and by [[lem-tensoring-a-projective-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-is-projective]] it sends projectives to projectives. A **projective functor** on $\mathcal O_\lambda$ is an endofunctor of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ isomorphic to a direct summand of some $F_E$; the full additive subcategory of all such functors (with arbitrary natural transformations as morphisms) is written $\mathcal F_\lambda$. It is closed under finite direct sums, composition, direct summands and passage to adjoints: composition corresponds to $F_E F_{E'}\cong F_{E\otimes E'}$, and $F_{E^*}$ is both a left and a right adjoint of $F_E$, by the published biadjunction for tensoring with duals. Every projective functor is exact and preserves projective objects. This is the definition of [BGe] and [Soe90, Section 1.2]; unlike the functors $T_\lambda^\mu$ of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], projective functors are not required to come from a single finite-dimensional tensor functor, only from a summand of one.
items.strategy: All closure properties are inherited from the published tensor and block-projection items: exactness and preservation of projective objects, additivity, and the adjunction for $E^*\otimes-$; direct summands of exact functors are exact after splitting, and the idempotent-completion convention for additive categories is [[def-additive-category]]. The composition identity is the associativity of the tensor product of finite-dimensional modules. No choice is used beyond the inherited AC of the block theory.

items.title: The coinvariant algebra is a complete intersection with one-dimensional socle
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published invariant-theory items. Let $w_1,\dots,w_r$ be homogeneous basic invariants of the finite Weyl group $W$ acting on $\mathfrak h$, of page degrees $2d_1,\dots,2d_r$ so that $d_1,\dots,d_r$ are the classical basic degrees (the degrees with $\deg\mathfrak h=1$; in the type-A model $d_1,\dots,d_r=1,\dots,n$), $S(\mathfrak h)^W=\mathbb C[w_1,\dots,w_r]$, and $\rho$ is the quotient by the ideal $I=(w_1,\dots,w_r)$. Put $N:=\sum_{i=1}^r(d_i-1)$; the top degree of the coinvariant algebra $C$ of [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]] is then $2N$. Then: (1) $w_1,\dots,w_r$ is a homogeneous regular sequence in $S$ and $C$ is a complete intersection: $C=S/(w_1,\dots,w_r)$ with $\operatorname{Hilb}(C,t)=\prod_i(1-t^{2d_i})/(1-t^2)^r$, $\dim C_{2N}=1$, $C_j=0$ for $j>2N$; (2) the multiplication pairing $C_i\times C_{2N-i}\to C_{2N}\cong\mathbb C$ is nondegenerate for every $i$, and consequently the socle $\operatorname{soc}(C)=\{c\in C: C_+c=0\}$ equals $C_{2N}$ and is one dimensional; (3) equivalently, $C$ is a graded Gorenstein algebra whose socle sits in the top degree $2N$.
items.strategy: The basic invariant regular sequence gives the Koszul free resolution of C and the displayed Hilbert series. Compute Tor_r^S(C,k) in two ways. Tensor the invariant Koszul resolution with k: all differentials vanish, so its top homology is the one-dimensional k in degree sum_i 2d_i. Tensor instead the Koszul resolution of k on the r degree-two polynomial variables with C: its top homology consists exactly of the elements killed by every variable, namely socle(C), shifted by 2r. The two Koszul calculations compute the same Tor (or use the finite free double Koszul complex and its two augmentations), so the socle is one-dimensional in degree 2sum_i(d_i-1)=2N. For nonzero homogeneous c, its nonzero ideal cC contains a nonzero element of maximal degree; multiplying that element by any positive variable is zero, hence it lies in this top socle. Thus c has a complementary-degree multiplier with nonzero product. This proves nondegeneracy of the top multiplication pairing on both sides; finite dimensions give perfectness. No dimension-symmetry shortcut or incorrect Ext-without-canonical-module shift is used.

items.title: The harmonic complement of the coinvariant algebra
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published invariant-theory items. Let $W$ act on $\mathfrak h$ by reflections and on $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ by graded algebra automorphisms, with coinvariant algebra $C=S/I$ as in [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]. Then there is a $W$-stable graded subspace $\mathcal H\subseteq S$ such that the multiplication map $$S^W\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathcal H\longrightarrow S,\qquad p\otimes h\mapsto ph,$$ is an isomorphism of graded $S^W$-modules and $W$-modules, and the restriction of the quotient map $\rho:S\to C$ to $\mathcal H$ is an isomorphism of graded $W$-modules $\mathcal H\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }C$. One may take $\mathcal H=\{f\in S:\partial_p f=0\text{ for all }p\in S^W_+\}$ for the $W$-equivariant Laplacian attached to a $W$-invariant positive definite form on $\mathfrak h_{\mathbb R}$, or any $W$-stable graded complement of $I$; in particular $\dim\mathcal H_d=\dim C_d$ for all $d$, $\dim\mathcal H=|W|$.
items.strategy: Choose a positive definite $W$-invariant real form on $\mathfrak h$ (finiteness of $W$ allows averaging an arbitrary positive definite real form); extend it to a positive definite Hermitian form on each finite-dimensional graded piece $S_d$ for which the adjoint of multiplication is differentiation. Because $I$ and $S^W_+$ are $W$-stable and the form is $W$-invariant, the orthogonal complement $\mathcal H_d:=I_d^{\perp}$ is $W$-stable and $S_d=I_d\oplus\mathcal H_d$; hence $\mathcal H$ is a graded $W$-submodule and the restriction of $\rho$ is injective with image spanned by $\mathcal H$, giving $\mathcal H\cong C$ as graded $W$-modules. The isomorphism $S^W\otimes\mathcal H\to S$ follows by comparing graded ranks: $S$ is free of rank $|W|$ over $S^W$ by [[thm-chevalley-shephard-todd-for-finite-weyl-groups]], the map is $S^W$-linear and graded, and modulo $S^W_+$ it reduces to the isomorphism $\mathcal H\to C$ induced by $\rho$; graded Nakayama over the graded-local ring $S^W$ makes it surjective, and the rank count (both sides are free of rank $|W|$ over $S^W$) makes it injective. This is the reflection-group case of the harmonic-complement argument used on the published $S(\mathfrak g)$-page; only finite-dimensional linear algebra and the published freeness are used.

items.title: The deformed category O family over the Cartan symmetric algebra
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ be the symmetric algebra of the Cartan subalgebra, graded by $\deg\mathfrak h=2$, and let $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$ act on $S\otimes\mathbb C_\lambda$ by $x\cdot(s\otimes1)=xs\otimes1+\lambda(x)s\otimes1$ for $x\in\mathfrak h$ and $x\cdot(s\otimes1)=xs\otimes1$ for $x\in\mathfrak n^+$, where $xs$ denotes the action of $\mathfrak b	o\mathfrak h$ on $S$ by weight. Put $M_S(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}(S\otimes\mathbb C_\lambda)\in \mathfrak g\otimes S$-mod, with the right $S$-module structure by multiplication on the last factor, so that $M_S(\lambda)\otimes_S\mathbb C_\epsilon\cong M(\lambda+\epsilon)$ for every $\epsilon\in\mathfrak h^*$. For a localization $T$ of $S$ put $M_T(\lambda):=M_S(\lambda)\otimes_S T$ and let $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ be the full subcategory of $\mathfrak g\otimes T$-modules that are direct summands of a finite direct sum of modules $E\otimes M_T(\lambda)$ for finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-modules $E$; write $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ for the localization $R=S_{(0)}$ at the origin of $\operatorname{Spec} S$. The **deformed family** is the assignment $T\mapsto\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ together with the specialization functors $-\otimes_T\mathbb C_\epsilon$ at the closed points $\epsilon$ of $\operatorname{Spec} T$; the specializations have Verma constituents with highest weights $\lambda+
u+\epsilon$, where $
u$ runs through the finite-dimensional tensor weights, and can meet several central-character blocks; a generic parameter is generally nonintegral, and the Verma constituents generically have distinct central characters except for repeated identical labels. For a regular dominant integral source $\lambda$ and any dot-dominant integral target $
u$ (so $
u+ho$ is in the closed positive chamber), denote by $\mathcal D_R^{[
u]}(\lambda)$ the component of $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ whose closed fiber lies in the selected target block $\mathcal O_
u$; finite Verma flags and pairwise-unit resultants of their central-character polynomials define this component by actual central idempotents over $R$. Other central-character components remain part of the full tensor family. Modules in $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ carry an $\mathfrak h$-weight decomposition with locally free finite-rank weight spaces. The conventions are those of [Soe90, Section 2.1].
items.strategy: The construction is the standard universal family of Verma modules with a formal deformation parameter; the twisted $\mathfrak b$-action makes the fiber at $\epsilon$ the Verma module of weight $\lambda+\epsilon$, the right $S$-action commutes with $\mathfrak g$, and direct summands of finite tensor products give the analogue of the projective functors of [[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]] over $T$. Weight spaces are locally free by the PBW model of Verma modules; no choice beyond the inherited AC of the block theory is used. Tensor products have finite Verma flags by the PBW tensor identity and the weight filtration of the finite-dimensional b-module E; the deformed flag factors are M_T(lambda+nu). Direct-summand flags over local R follow by canonical maximal-weight peeling: U(g)X^nu=Delta_R(nu) tensor_R X^nu for a maximal label, every idempotent preserves this submodule, its top-weight image is finite free, and induction applies to the quotient. For selected components choose a central element separating the finitely many special central characters of these factors; its grouped annihilating polynomials have pairwise-unit resultants and hence Chinese-remainder projectors in R[X], which become actual central projectors. Thus whole-family statements and selected-block statements are distinguished. The generic regular/nonintegral Verma assertion follows from the Shapovalov determinant factors; generic here means the generic point or parameters avoiding the countably many reducibility hyperplanes, not a Zariski-open set on which integrality persists.

items.title: The nilpotent central fiber is reduced and integral
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let p_1,...,p_r be homogeneous basic generators of S(g)^g for complex semisimple g, corresponding by Chevalley restriction to basic Weyl invariants. Then $$A=S(g)/(p_1,\ldots,p_r)$$ is a reduced integral domain of dimension dim g-r=2|Phi^+|, with Hilbert series product_i(1-t^{d_i})/(1-t)^{dim g}. For every central character chi, the PBW associated graded of U(g)/U(g)ker chi is canonically A.
items.strategy: For g=0, A=C and the assertions are immediate; below use the nonzero semisimple case. Invariant-ring freeness makes p_i a regular sequence, so A is a complete intersection with the displayed Hilbert series; polynomial rings and their regular-sequence quotients are Cohen-Macaulay locally. Construct the principal triple e=sum e_i, h=2rho^vee, f=sum c_i f_i where h=sum c_i h_i. The simple root triples and invertible Cartan matrix give [h,e]=2e,[h,f]=-2f,[e,f]=h. Complete reducibility restricts the adjoint module to a sum of sl2 strings. Since ad h has only even eigenvalues and zero space the r-dimensional Cartan, there are r strings L_{2m_j}; no trivial string exists because a Cartan vector commuting with all simple e_i is zero. Thus m_j>0, sum m_j=|Phi^+|, ker ad e has dimension r and lies in n_+, and g=[g,e] direct-sum ker ad f. Let z_f=ker ad f, with lowest-string coordinates y_j. The restrictions q_i(y)=p_i(e+y) are algebraically independent: compose root-unipotent polynomial exponentials and diagonal root-character torus maps, acting on e+z_f. Choose dim[g,e] basis directions with independent commutators with e; together with z_f the coordinate map has nonzero square Jacobian at the origin. It is dominant: a polynomial relation of least degree on its image, differentiated through the generically invertible Jacobian, would have all its lower-degree partial derivatives zero, hence be constant in characteristic zero. Invariance would transfer any relation among q_i to that dense image and then to the algebraically independent p_i. The action x->t Ad(t^{-rho^vee})x fixes e and gives y_j weight m_j+1, so q_i is weighted-homogeneous of degree d_i. Algebraic independence in r variables implies its Jacobian is not identically zero: the fraction field C(y) is finite separable over C(q), and differentiating the minimal polynomials expresses the dy_j in the span of dq_i. Its determinant has weighted degree sum d_i-sum(m_j+1)=0 by the degree-sum lemma. All weights are positive, so this determinant is a nonzero constant. Thus dp_i(e) are independent; this supplies the missing Kostant-slice deduction rather than assuming individual degrees match the exponents. For the underlying zero set, put G=Aut(g)^0, an affine algebraic group defined by bracket preservation, smooth by Cartier in characteristic zero, with Lie algebra Der(g)=ad g. The diagonal root-character torus H and N_+=exp(ad n_+) are closed connected algebraic subgroups (exponential/logarithm and BCH are finite polynomials in the positive-height nilpotent matrices). H N_+ is a Borel: its Lie algebra b is maximal solvable, since any negative-root component in a larger algebra, isolated by Cartan weight projectors, supplies a root sl2 with b. A nilpotent ad x exponentiates to a connected unipotent subgroup contained in a Borel; Borel conjugacy puts x in b, and its Cartan component must vanish because otherwise ad x has a nonzero root eigenvalue. Hence every nilpotent is conjugate into n_+. Conversely all p_i vanish on n_+ by the contracting root torus. If all p_i vanish, all invariant traces Tr((ad x)^k) vanish; Newton identities make ad x nilpotent. The zero set is therefore the image of G times n_+, hence irreducible (smooth connected group varieties are irreducible). It is the closure of the principal orbit: in positive-height grading ad e:n_{+,k}->n_{+,k+1} is onto by the sl2 strings, so successive exponentials exp(ad x_k) prescribe each higher-height coefficient of e, and the torus prescribes nonzero simple coefficients; the Borel orbit contains the dense subset of n_+ with all simple coefficients nonzero. The nonradical-ideal clause of the published affine Jacobian criterion makes A regular at e, since its local dimension is dim g-r. Invariance makes the dense principal orbit regular, so A is generically reduced. For any associated prime q of A, its localization has depth0; local Cohen-Macaulayness gives dimension0, hence q is minimal. Irreducibility leaves one minimal prime, whose generic localization is a field by generic regularity. The published associated-prime detection map injects A into this field, proving reducedness and the domain assertion. Finally the filtered harmonic Z-free decomposition of U gives gr(U/ker chi)=Sg/(p_i): the leading central generators are p_i and specialization of the filtered free harmonic basis has exactly the quotient Hilbert series, so the natural graded surjection is an isomorphism. This works componentwise for semisimple g, not only type A.

items.title: The wall-crossing functor and its unit and counit
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the dominant regular integral block representative $\lambda$ and an integral highest weight $\mu$ such that $\lambda+\rho$ is regular dominant and $\mu+\rho$ is dominant with dot stabilizer exactly $\{1,s\}$. This is the dominant-chamber version of single-wall data; the published datum uses antidominant representatives. Take the finite-dimensional simple $E$ with extremal weight $\mu-\lambda$, and define onto-wall translation $T_{\mathrm{on}}=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\mu}(E\otimes-)$ and out-of-wall translation $T_{\mathrm{out}}=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}(E^*\otimes-)$. The wall-crossing functor is $\theta_s=T_{\mathrm{out}}T_{\mathrm{on}}$. It is an exact projective functor, a natural direct summand of tensoring by $E^*\otimes E$ followed by regular block projection. The two tensor-block adjunctions give $\eta:\operatorname{id}\to\theta_s$ and $\varepsilon:\theta_s\to\operatorname{id}$; each belongs to its corresponding adjunction pair and satisfies the triangle identities with the companion unit or counit on the wall category. Up to natural equivalence the functor depends only on the wall and the block; the chosen biadjunction maps remain part of the data.
items.strategy: Exactness and biadjunction follow from finite-dimensional tensor-Hom pairing and exact central block inclusion/projection. The singular block projection is a natural idempotent on E tensor -, so composing it with E* tensor - gives the asserted summand of a single tensor functor. The dominant-chamber standard counts are proved by the general dominant norm-distance and extremal-weight bound, not by applying the printed antidominant-only datum literally. Their two-factor class on the dominant Verma is Delta_e+Delta_s. BGG reciprocity and the one-dimensional simple-root lowered weight give P_s the same flag; hence theta_s Delta_e=P_s. The later proved projective-functor classification lifts equality of these evaluations to natural equivalence, proving wall-weight independence. This is a forward well-definedness discharge, declared in justified_by, not a circular prerequisite for chosen-wall construction or object generation.

items.title: The coinvariant algebra is the graded regular representation of W
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published invariant-theory items. Let $W$ be a finite Weyl group with reflection representation $\mathfrak h$, coinvariant algebra $C=S(\mathfrak h)/S(\mathfrak h)S^W_+$ and basic degrees $d_1,\dots,d_r$ as in [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]. Then: (1) $C\cong\mathbb C W$ as a $W$-module: $C$ is isomorphic to the regular representation of $W$; (2) the graded $W$-character of $C$ is $$\operatorname{HTr}(C,t)(w):=\sum_{i\ge0}t^{i}\operatorname{tr}(w\mid C_i)=\prod_{i=1}^r(1-t^{2d_i})\cdot\det(1-t^2w\mid\mathfrak h^*)^{-1}\qquad(w\in W),$$ where $d_1,\dots,d_r$ are the classical basic degrees of [[lem-the-coinvariant-algebra-is-a-gorenstein-algebra-with-one-dimensional-socle]], an identity of rational functions whose value at $t=1$ is $|W|$ for $w=1$ and $0$ for $w\neq1$; (3) equivalently, $C$ is the graded lift of the regular representation: writing $\operatorname{mult}_E(C,t)$ for the graded multiplicity of the irreducible $W$-module $E$, the identity $\sum_E\operatorname{mult}_E(C,t)\,\chi_E(w)=\operatorname{HTr}(C,t)(w)$ determines the graded multiplicities uniquely, with $\operatorname{mult}_E(C,1)=\dim E$ the multiplicity of $E$ in the regular representation. The Hilbert-series specialization of (2) at $w=1$ is $\prod_i(1+t^2+\dots+t^{2(d_i-1)})$, the published formula in the page's $\deg\mathfrak h=2$ normalization.
items.strategy: By [[lem-the-harmonic-complement-of-the-coinvariant-algebra]] the quotient map restricts to an isomorphism $\mathcal H\cong C$ of graded $W$-modules with $S=S^W\otimes\mathcal H$, so $\operatorname{HTr}(C,t)=\operatorname{HTr}(\mathcal H,t)$ and, since $S^W$ contributes the scalar factor $\prod_i(1-t^{2d_i})^{-1}$ to the graded trace of $S$, the identities of the published Hilbert-series lemma give $\operatorname{HTr}(C,t)=\operatorname{HTr}(S,t)\cdot\prod_i(1-t^{2d_i})$ with $\operatorname{HTr}(S,t)(w)=\det(1-t^2w|\mathfrak h^*)^{-1}$ (Molien's formula, proved there). For (1): evaluate at $t\to1$. The numerator vanishes to order exactly $r$ and the denominator to order $\dim\mathfrak h^w$; for $w\neq1$ the reflection representation is faithful, so $\dim\mathfrak h^w\le\dim\mathfrak h-1=r-1$ and the numerator order exceeds the denominator order, giving limit $0$ for $w\neq1$; at $w=1$ the limit is $\prod_i d_i=|W|$ by the published dimension formula. A finite-dimensional $\mathbb C$-representation is determined up to isomorphism by its character, so $C\cong\mathbb C W$ as $W$-modules. Part (3) is the standard description of graded $W$-modules by their graded characters and Krull-Schmidt uniqueness for the semisimple category of finite-dimensional $W$-modules over $\mathbb C$. The computation is choice-free except for the inherited AC of the published Hilbert-series lemma.

items.title: The antidominant projective and the Soergel functor
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. In the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ of [[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] fix the antidominant weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$ and let $P:=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ be a projective cover of $L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$; it is unique up to isomorphism and indecomposable by [[prop-projective-covers-in-o-are-indecomposable-and-unique]], and it is an injective object of $\mathcal O_\lambda$. The **Soergel functor** is $$V:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,-)\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow \operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)^{\mathrm{op}}\text{-mod},\qquad M\longmapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,M),$$ with the action of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ induced by composition of endomorphisms of $P$. Its values on the standard objects and on the indecomposable projectives are written $V\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):=V(\Delta(w\cdot\lambda))$ and $VP(w\cdot\lambda):=V(P(w\cdot\lambda))$; the choice of projective cover changes $V$ by a natural equivalence only. The functor is exact, and hence left exact, and $VP\cong\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ with the regular module structure.
items.strategy:
Injectivity has the following algebraic proof using only published suppliers. Put $\eta=-ho$. Every simple in its central-character summand has highest weight in $W\cdot\eta=\{\eta\}$, by highest-weight classification and the central-character theorem. Thus $M(\eta)=L(\eta)$: its top weight has dimension one and its finite composition series has only this simple. BGG reciprocity and a Verma flag give $P(\eta)=L(\eta)$; enough projectives then makes this one-simple block semisimple, so $L(\eta)$ is also injective. Let $E=L(\lambda+ho)$ and set $Q=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}(E\otimes L(\eta))$. The general tensor-block exact biadjunction proved in [[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]] shows that $Q$ is projective and injective. Set $a=w_0\cdot\lambda=w_0(\lambda+ho)-ho$. The same central-orbit/top-weight argument makes the antidominant $M(a)$ simple (any other highest weight in its dot orbit is strictly above $a$). Tensoring $E^*\otimes M(a)$ has a Verma flag with factors $M(a+
u)$ indexed by weights $
u$ of $E^*$. Projection to $\chi_\eta$ retains only $a+
u=-ho$, namely $
u=-w_0(\lambda+ho)$, the highest weight of $E^*$ of multiplicity one. Hence that projection is $L(\eta)$, and adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,L(a))=\mathbb C$. Lift the surjection $Q	o L(a)$ through the projective cover $P(a)	o L(a)$; essentiality of the cover makes the lift surjective, and projectivity of $P(a)$ splits it. Thus $P(a)$ is a summand of the injective $Q$ and is injective. This proof does not assume the Endomorphismensatz. Projectivity also makes $V$ exact (and hence left exact); independence of the chosen cover and $VP=\operatorname{End}(P)$ follow directly by composition and projective-cover uniqueness. In fact $Q=P(a)$: its projected tensor Verma flag consists of every $\Delta(x\cdot\lambda)$ once, since the retained E-weights are exactly the distinct extremal weights $x(\lambda+ho)$, all of multiplicity one. The published Verma embedding criterion embeds the simple $\Delta(a)=L(a)$ in every standard in the block, so BGG reciprocity makes every standard multiplicity in $P(a)$ at least one. Since $P(a)$ is a summand of the once-each flag of $Q$, all these multiplicities are exactly one and the complementary summand has no flag factors, hence is zero.

items.title: Duflo–Joseph g-finite endomorphisms of every Verma module
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every highest weight mu of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra, the action induces an algebra isomorphism $$U(g)/U(g)\ker\chi_\mu\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ (\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}M(\mu))^{\mathrm{ad}\,g\text{-finite}}.$$ In particular Ann M(mu)=U(g)ker chi_mu. For every finite-dimensional E, dim Hom_g(M(mu),E tensor M(mu))=dim E_0, and the action identifies each finite adjoint isotypic multiplicity with that dimension.
items.strategy: If g=0 then U=M=C and all assertions are immediate; below assume N>0. First expand the field dimension argument. A finite-length Verma has a simple submodule L(eta); the universal highest-weight map M(eta)->M(mu) is injective, hence factors through a simple only if M(eta)=L(eta). Thus it has a simple Verma submodule. For a simple Verma M, restricted duality identifies D M=M. Tensor adjunction and the standard/costandard Hom–Ext vanishing compute Hom(M,E tensor D M)=Hom(E* tensor M,D M), whose dimension is the number of its M-standard factors, dim E_0. For arbitrary M(mu), the same Hom is the kernel of finitely many simple-raising equations on the finite PBW weight space (E tensor M(mu))_mu. Their matrices are polynomial in mu, so dimension is at least its generic simple-Verma value dim E_0. Let M(eta) subset M(mu) be the simple Verma just found. Its embedding as a left U(n_-) module is right multiplication u->u p by a nonzero singular PBW element p in U(n_-). The quotient has filtered growth O(n^{N-1}), N=dim n_-, because its associated graded is a quotient of the polynomial ring by the nonzero leading element, whose Hilbert series is (1-t^d)/(1-t)^N. Tensoring a finite-dimensional module preserves this growth bound. Hence a map M(mu)->E tensor M(mu) must take M(eta) into E tensor M(eta), since otherwise the simple source embeds in a module of that smaller growth. Restriction to M(eta) is injective: a map killing it factors through the smaller-growth quotient into the free U(n_-)-module E tensor M(mu). Freeness follows from the Hopf tensor identity u tensor v -> sum u_(1)m_mu tensor u_(2)v, whose inverse uses the antipode. Any nonzero vector in that finite free module generates a free copy of the PBW domain and has growth n^N, impossible for such a quotient image. Restriction thus bounds the original Hom by dim E_0, proving equality. For action injectivity, let v be the highest vector of the simple Verma M(eta) inside M(mu). Its Shapovalov pairing U(n_+)_beta times U(n_-)_(-beta)->C is perfect in every weight. In a nonzero x=sum_beta x_beta in U(n_-) tensor U(n_+), choose a minimal beta with x_beta=sum_i b_i tensor a_i nonzero and act on a dual PBW vector a_j^*v. All other terms vanish by highest-weight support and minimality; the result is b_j v, nonzero for some j. Therefore multiplication followed by action injects this 2N-dimensional PBW-growth space into the image of the central reduction. If the action kernel in U_chi were nonzero, its nonzero homogeneous graded ideal in the proved domain A would contain a principal nonzero homogeneous ideal A f. Multiplication by f is injective, and the complete-intersection Hilbert series shows the cumulative growth of A/(f) is O(n^{2N-1}), whereas the injected PBW subspace has growth bounded below by a positive multiple of n^{2N}. This contradiction proves action injectivity. Finally its E-isotypic source has dimension dim E_0 by the adjoint multiplicity lemma and its target has the same dimension by the field Hom calculation. The injective map is therefore onto each isotypic, and local finiteness/complete reducibility of the adjoint action gives the full algebra isomorphism. No unproved annihilator equality, nilpotent-cone reducedness or arbitrary-weight generic inference is used. For the generic kernel lower bound, simple-Verma weights are Zariski dense: a proper submodule has a minimal-positive-height singular vector of weight mu-beta. Equal quadratic Casimir scalars give 2(mu+rho,beta)=(beta,beta), impossible throughout the real negative chamber. This real open set is Zariski dense, and meets the maximal-rank open locus of the finite polynomial raising matrix. Kernel dimension there is dimE0, so at every weight the kernel dimension is at least dimE0. The existing restriction and growth upper bound remains unchanged.

items.title: Wall-crossing acts on standard modules by a two-step extension
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. Let $\theta_s$ be the wall-crossing functor of [[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] attached to the simple reflection $s$ in the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$. For every $w\in W$ the object $\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ has a finite Verma flag with exactly two factors, namely $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ and $\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)$, each with multiplicity one; in the Grothendieck group $$[\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]=[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)].$$ Moreover the functor is exact and preserves Verma-filtered objects and finite Verma flags: if $X$ has a finite Verma flag with multiplicities $(X:\Delta(v\cdot\lambda))$, then $\theta_s X$ has one with multiplicity $(\theta_s X:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))=(X:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))+(X:\Delta(us\cdot\lambda))$, and the same formula holds for the images in the Grothendieck group. This is the wall-crossing computation of [Soe90, Section 2.1] in the form supplied by the published wall-translation theorem; the resulting flag is not in general split, but splitting is not asserted or used here.
items.strategy: Use the finite-dimensional tensor weight filtration and the norm comparison: translating a regular standard onto the s-wall retains precisely the one singular standard at the same coset, and translating it out retains the two regular labels w and ws, once each. The dominant-representative convention is established directly by the same published dominant norm-distance and extremal-weight argument (the printed single-wall datum uses antidominant representatives); changing to the dominant orbit representative reverses Bruhat labels. Exactness concatenates these two-factor flags across a finite Verma flag of X, proving the stated multiplicity formula. The two-step object need not split. No assertion that arbitrary subquotients of Verma-filtered objects are Verma-filtered is used.

items.title: Base change, freeness and specialization in the deformed family
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. In the deformed family of [[def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-its-specializations]] with $T$ a localization of $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ and $M,N\in\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$: (1) the canonical map $$U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_Z T\longrightarrow \big(\operatorname{End}_T(M_T(\lambda))\big)^{\mathfrak g\text{-finite}},\qquad u\otimes t\longmapsto\big(m\mapsto u\cdot m\cdot t\big),$$ is an isomorphism of $T$-algebras, the superscript denoting the $\mathfrak g$-finite part for the adjoint action $X\cdot f=X\circ f-f\circ X$, and $Z=Z(U(\mathfrak g))$ acting on $T$ through the published shifted Harish-Chandra isomorphism $\operatorname{HC}_\rho$ followed by evaluation at $\lambda+\rho+\epsilon$ on the universal parameter $\epsilon$; (2) $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(E\otimes M_T(\lambda),F\otimes M_T(\lambda))$ is a free $T$-module of rank $\dim(E\otimes F^*)_0$ for finite-dimensional $E,F$, where the subscript denotes the zero weight space, and the natural base-change map $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(M,N)\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes\kappa(\epsilon)}(M\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon),N\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon))$$ is an isomorphism for every $\epsilon\in\operatorname{Spec} T$, with residue field $\kappa(\epsilon)$; (3) $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(M,N)$ is locally free of finite rank over $T$; (4) if a $\mathfrak g\otimes R$-linear map of objects of $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ is an isomorphism on the special fiber at $0$, it is an isomorphism (Nakayama).
items.strategy: Use the locally proved Duflo–Joseph theorem in every field fiber and the exact adjoint zero-weight-rank lemma. For each finite-dimensional E, Hom(M_S(lambda),E tensor M_S(lambda)) is the kernel of the finitely many simple-raising maps on the finite free relative lambda-weight space; PBW bases make their matrices polynomial in the parameter. Every closed fiber has dimension dim E_0 by the field theorem. Thus every (s+1)-minor vanishes and the s-minors generate the unit ideal, where s is the constant matrix rank: vanishing follows from polynomial evaluation at all complex points, and a proper minor ideal would lie in a maximal ideal. On each invertible s-minor chart, Gaussian elimination puts the matrix in diag(I_s,0), proving that its kernel is finite projective, locally split and commutes with every base change, including residue fields of nonclosed primes. Tensor adjunction identifies this kernel with the appropriate finite adjoint isotypic endomorphisms. The action source is finite free of the same zero-weight rank by harmonic isotypic freeness; its closed-fiber maps are the Duflo–Joseph isomorphisms, so its finite cokernel vanishes by local Nakayama at every maximal ideal, and the equal-rank projective kernel vanishes as well. Hence action is an isomorphism on every isotypic over S and, by local finiteness, on all g-finite endomorphisms. The same finite matrices and flat localization give every T localization. For tensor objects E tensor M and F tensor M, adjunction reduces Hom to the same finite highest-weight kernel for E* tensor F, proving the stated rank and specialization. Direct summands take images of split idempotents in these Hom modules, preserving finite projectivity/local freeness and all base-change isomorphisms. Over local R the weight spaces are finite free; a g⊗R-linear residue isomorphism is invertible weight by weight by the determinant/Nakayama argument. This algebraic route replaces the imported universal differential-operator theorem and the Jantzen7.25 fallback without dropping any all-T or all-weight assertion.

items.title: The wall-crossing action on the Grothendieck group is multiplication by 1+s
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. In the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ of [[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] the assignment $$c\colon K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z[W],\qquad [\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]\longmapsto w,$$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups, and for every simple reflection $s$ the wall-crossing functor $\theta_s$ of [[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] satisfies $$c\,[\theta_s X]=c\,[X]\cdot(1+s)\qquad\text{for all }X\in\mathcal O_\lambda,$$ i.e. right multiplication by $1+s$ in the integral group ring $\mathbb Z[W]$. Consequently $c$ intertwines the wall-crossing action with the right regular action of $\mathbb Z[W]$ generated by the elements $1+s$; in particular for a reduced word $w=s_1\cdots s_k$, one has $c[\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}\Delta(\lambda)]=(1+s_1)\cdots(1+s_k)$, the sum of all subexpression products with their actual multiplicities; its top Bruhat term is $w$ once and all other terms have smaller labels. With the displayed composition $\theta_{s_1}\cdots\theta_{s_k}$ instead, the factors are multiplied in the reverse order.
items.strategy: The class of any object is the sum of the classes of the factors of a finite Verma flag, and [[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]] gives that the Verma classes form a basis; since the block has $|W|$ Verma classes indexed by $W$, the assignment is an isomorphism of free abelian groups. The formula $[\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]=[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)]$ of [[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-standard-modules-by-the-two-step-extension]], applied factor by factor using exactness of $\theta_s$, gives $c[\theta_s X]=c[X]\cdot(1+s)$ on the Verma basis, hence on the whole group; the right multiplication by $s$ acts by $w\mapsto ws$ on the basis, giving the displayed convention. Composition applies its rightmost functor first, so iteration gives the reverse functor order and the product of (1+s_i), not the single group element w. The full reduced subexpression is the unique one of maximal length; proper subexpressions have smaller Bruhat labels, with multiplicities that can exceed one.

items.title: Wall-crossing compositions produce the projective with the top standard label
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a dominant regular integral representative $\lambda$ and reduced word $w=s_1\cdots s_k$, set $\theta_{\underline w}=\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}$, so the standards follow right multiplication in word order. Then $$\theta_{\underline w}\Delta(\lambda)\cong P(w\cdot\lambda)\oplus\bigoplus_{x<w}P(x\cdot\lambda)^{m_x},\qquad m_x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.$$ Its class is $(1+s_1)\cdots(1+s_k)$ under the standard class map, with actual subexpression multiplicities. The BGG matrix satisfies $(P(x\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=[\Delta(y\cdot\lambda):L(x\cdot\lambda)]$, vanishes unless $y\le x$ in Bruhat order, and has diagonal entries one. Hence the top summand $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ occurs once and is the only summand whose flag contains $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$; the remaining multiplicities are determined by this triangular matrix and the product class. Consequently every indecomposable projective is a summand of a word of wall crossings applied to $\Delta(\lambda)$.
items.strategy: The dominant Verma is projective in its block, since its Hom functor is its maximal weight space; exact biadjoint wall crossing preserves projectives. Thus the word object decomposes into indecomposable projective covers. Its standard class is the subexpression product from the corrected right-action lemma. The full reduced subexpression contributes w once and all other subexpressions are below w. Strong linkage and BGG reciprocity give the Bruhat-triangular projective matrix with standard support y<=x and diagonal one for the dominant representative. A maximal head outside the class support would contribute its own standard with positive coefficient, impossible, so only x<=w occur. The coefficient of Delta_w forces P_w once. The remaining coefficients are determined successively. Nonnegativity follows from the actual projective decomposition, not an assumed all-one interval character. Explicitly, a strong-linkage reflection with positive integral pairing sends a dominant-orbit label x to s_alpha x with larger Bruhat label, by the positive-root reflection-descent criterion and subword/deletion property. This proves the required reversal of the weight order and the Bruhat standard-support triangle; proper subexpressions reduce by deletion to subwords of w.

items.title: Lifting of indecomposable projectives to the deformed family
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be dominant regular integral, $R=S(\mathfrak h)_{(0)}$, and use the selected component $\mathcal D_R^{[\lambda]}(\lambda)$ of the tensor-generated deformed family. For every $x\in W$ there is a projective $P_R(x,\lambda)$ in the deformed $\lambda$ block whose residue fiber is $P(x\cdot\lambda)$. It is unique up to isomorphism; every indecomposable of this selected tensor component is one of these lifts. Each lift has a finite deformed Verma flag with the same multiplicities as its closed fiber. More generally, a finite projective in this block is a direct summand of a finite sum of the truncated induced projectives representing relative weight spaces; for every map of deformation algebras $R	o R'$ its base change is projective in the corresponding truncated category, and $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_R}(P,N)\otimes_R R'\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{R'}}(P\otimes_R R',N\otimes_R R').$$ For a finite Verma-filtered target $N$, this Hom module is finite free over local $R$. A g⊗R-linear map between such finite projective/Verma-filtered objects whose residue fiber is an isomorphism is itself an isomorphism, weight by weight. For a dot-dominant integral target $
u$, including singular $
u$, the same local projective construction gives all lifts in its deformed block, with labels the distinct cosets $W/W_
u$. These lifts belong to the target component $\mathcal D_R^{[
u]}(\lambda)$ of a regular-source tensor family; it is not necessary or asserted that the singular Verma itself generates every target projective. The full tensor family, including other central components, is not claimed to have only these indecomposables.
items.strategy:
Use the independent local construction recorded in the owner proof note, rather than the universal g-finite endomorphism theorem. For $\xi\le\lambda$, truncate the positive PBW weights of $U(\mathfrak b)$ above $\lambda-\xi$, tensor its finite right-$U(\mathfrak h)$-free quotient with the deformed rank-one weight $\xi$, and induce to $\mathfrak g$. The resulting $Q_R(\xi)$ has a finite Verma flag and represents the weight functor $N\mapsto N^\xi$ on weights $\le\lambda$: evaluate at the cyclic tensor generator; all excluded positive monomials kill a vector of weight $\xi$. Thus it is projective and its Hom functor commutes with arbitrary algebra base change. The same holds for finite sums and direct summands, by taking images of split weight-space idempotents. To isolate a central component, choose $z$ separating the finitely many special characters in the flag. Group its annihilating factors $X-\operatorname{HC}_ho(z)(
u+ho+	au)$ by special character. Pairwise resultants are units of $R$; the Sylvester adjugate supplies Bezout identities, and Chinese remaindering yields actual polynomial central projectors over $R$. No completion is assumed. A direct summand of a local deformed Verma flag is Verma-filtered: for a maximal label $
u$, the canonical submodule $U(\mathfrak g)X^
u=\Delta_R(
u)\otimes_R X^
u$ has Verma-filtered quotient. Prove this by induction on the original flag, splitting a last quotient labelled $
u$ by a lifted highest vector. Every projector preserves this canonical submodule; its top-weight image is finite free over local $R$, and induction on the quotient proves the assertion. Now induct orbit weights downward. The selected $Q_R(\xi)$ has special fiber containing $P(\xi)$ once and only $P(\eta)$ with $\eta>\xi$ otherwise, since $\operatorname{Hom}(Q_0(\xi),L(\eta))=L(\eta)^\xi$. Lift the inclusion and retraction of the already constructed higher-label sum using the proved projective Hom base-change law. Their composite is $1$ modulo the maximal ideal in a finite $R$-End algebra. Left and right multiplication by this composite have finite cokernels killed by Nakayama, so it has a two-sided inverse. Correct the retraction by that inverse and take the complementary projective summand; it specializes to $P(\xi)$. This constructs every lift; lifting inverse maps proves uniqueness by the same finite-End argument, and free flag quotients preserve multiplicities. Finite-dimensional tensoring and central projection are exact biadjoint functors over $R$ by the tensor-Hom pairing, so they preserve projectives. The dominant deformed Verma represents its top weight in its block. For the regular block, ordinary wall-word object generation is proved first from two-step flags and BGG. Its deformed word is projective and specializes to the same projective word, so local lift uniqueness identifies its summands with the constructed lifts. This proves membership in the fixed regular-source tensor family without invoking the later functor classifier. For a dot-dominant singular target nu, construct its lifts by the same truncated-projective induction. Choose sigma=nu+N rho regular dominant so large that sigma-mu is dominant for every mu in its finite orbit. Tensor M_R(sigma) with the finite-dimensional simple having lowest extremal weight mu-sigma. In its selected target component, all retained standard labels are at least mu and mu occurs once; BGG and projective decomposition therefore give P(mu) once. Projective Hom base change lifts that splitting to the constructed P_R(mu). Thus all singular lifts lie in the regular-source sigma tensor family. The dominant norm-distance argument translates the regular standard M_R(lambda) to M_R(sigma) with one retained factor and conversely, so the two tensor families agree: nested natural block projectors remain summands of the product finite-dimensional tensor. The singular target component has all these coset-labelled projectives, and its indecomposable objects are exactly them by lifting its finite residual projective decomposition. This is the true regular-source singular-target assertion. This proves the local projective interface; it does not prove the separate all-localizations universal-Verma Kostant assertion.

items.title: Indecomposable projective functors are indexed by the Weyl group
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral block with dominant representative $\lambda$: (1) projective functors form a Krull-Schmidt category; (2) their indecomposables are indexed by $W$, with $\Theta_w$ characterized by $\Theta_w\Delta(\lambda)\cong P(w\cdot\lambda)$. For any reduced word $w=s_1\cdots s_k$, $\Theta_w$ is a multiplicity-one summand of $\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}$ and every other indecomposable summand has a label $x<w$. In particular every indecomposable projective functor is generated as a summand by wall crossings. (3) Two projective functors are naturally equivalent exactly when their induced operators on the Grothendieck group agree. The characterization concerns evaluation on the dominant projective Verma.
items.strategy: Evaluation of natural maps on the dominant Verma is surjective, not necessarily injective on ordinary O. For ambient tensor functors, a map E tensor M(lambda)->F tensor M(lambda) is a finite adjoint matrix coefficient in End M(lambda); Duflo–Joseph identifies it with a g-equivariant matrix in U_chi. The harmonic isotypic free decomposition lifts that matrix to U, giving a U-bimodule map E tensor U->F tensor U and hence a natural tensor-functor map on all modules. Compose the exact block projections and summand inclusions/retractions to obtain surjectivity for all projective functors. The evaluation kernel is nilpotent: every standard Delta_y embeds in the dominant Delta_e, so exactness and naturality make a map vanishing on Delta_e vanish on every standard. On a fixed projective generator with a Verma flag of length k it strictly lowers the induced flag; k-fold compositions vanish. Evaluation at that generator is faithful for natural maps on exact functors because every object has a finite projective presentation. It also proves finite-dimensionality of natural End spaces. Hence the kernel on every finite additive functor sum is a nilpotent ideal. Idempotents lift across a nilpotent ideal by correcting a lift modulo successive powers (or the explicit polynomial idempotent-lifting formula); isomorphisms lift because 1 plus a nilpotent-kernel element is invertible by a finite geometric series. Therefore decompositions and isomorphism classes of projective functors are exactly those of their dominant-Verma evaluations. Finite-dimensional End algebras and split idempotents give Krull–Schmidt; indecomposable local End rings correspond through the nilpotent kernel. The corrected wall-word projective-generation lemma realizes every P_w and gives the new multiplicity-one functor Theta_w. If two K0 operators agree, their dominant-Verma evaluations are projectives with the same class, hence the same indecomposable multiplicities by BGG unitriangularity; lift their isomorphism to the functors. The converse is formal. Central nilpotent natural endomorphisms of the identity vanish on Delta_e, so no false full-faithfulness assertion for this evaluation is made.

items.title: The central action on the deformed antidominant projective
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be dominant regular integral, $S=S(\mathfrak h)$, $R=S_{(0)}$, and $P_R=P_R(w_0,\lambda)$ the deformed antidominant projective. Write $\operatorname{HC}_ho\colon Z(U(\mathfrak g))	o S^W$ for the published shifted Harish-Chandra isomorphism, $\sigma_\lambda(f)(\epsilon)=f(\lambda+ho+\epsilon)$, and define $$a_\lambda\colon Z\otimes_{\mathbb C}R\longrightarrow R\otimes_{R^W}R,\qquad z\otimes r\longmapsto\sigma_\lambda(\operatorname{HC}_ho(z))\otimes r.$$ Then $a_\lambda$ and the action map $Z\otimes R	o\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes R}(P_R)$ are surjective and have the same kernel, inducing a canonical $R$-algebra isomorphism $$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes R}(P_R)\cong R\otimes_{R^W}R.$$ On a generic Verma constituent of highest weight $x\cdot\lambda+\epsilon$, $z$ acts by the scalar $\operatorname{HC}_ho(z)(x(\lambda+ho)+\epsilon)=\sigma_\lambda(\operatorname{HC}_ho(z))(x^{-1}\epsilon)$; these scalars vary with $x$, and the center need not act by a single scalar on $P_R$. After tensoring the right $R$ factor with the residue field at $0$, the endomorphism algebra becomes $C=S/(S^W_+S)$. More generally, for dot-dominant integral $
u$ (meaning $
u+ho$ lies in the closed positive chamber) the corresponding algebra is $R^{W_
u}\otimes_{R^W}R$, where $W_
u$ is the dot stabilizer. Translation out of that facet identifies the singular antidominant projective with the regular one; under these shifted Harish-Chandra identifications, its induced endomorphism map is the inclusion $R^{W_
u}\otimes_{R^W}R\hookrightarrow R\otimes_{R^W}R$.
items.strategy: The complete algebraic local-order proof is recorded in the owner central-order note. First the most-singular translation Q has each distinct block Verma once. It contains P_antidominant as a split summand; every standard contains its simple antidominant Verma, so BGG reciprocity forces every flag multiplicity of P to be one and Q=P. The local projective theorem gives the same free flag for P_R and arbitrary Hom base change. Generically its constituents have distinct central characters and End(P_K) is the tuple algebra. At a height-one nonroot prime they remain distinct. At a root prime alpha, the residual central characters split into pairs {x,s_alpha x}, or singletons in the singular case. The symbolic generic-hyperplane Shapovalov/Casimir proof gives the upper Verma length2 and the lower Verma simple. The localized projective pair has those two flag factors once; its residue cannot split, since the lower simple Verma is nonprojective (dualizing the upper length2 Verma supplies a nonsplit extension ending in it). Any endomorphism preserves the maximal-weight Verma and has two scalar eigenvalues congruent mod alpha; otherwise its residual polynomial projector would split the extension. Their Casimir eigenvalues differ by n(alpha,alpha)tau(alpha^vee), a unit times the DVR parameter. Thus identity and Casimir generate precisely the full congruence order. Finite central polynomial projectors isolate different pairs. Independently R tensor_{R^W}R has the same local orders: CRT separates distinct graph branches, and a linear polynomial with nonzero root-normal coefficient generates the within-pair uniformizer difference. It is finite free by invariant freeness; taking first-factor stabilizer invariants gives the singular order. Both this order and End(P_R) are intersections of their height-one localizations in their generic tuple spaces, because they are finite free over the polynomial local ring. They therefore agree globally. To prove shifted central-image surjectivity, for H=Stab(nu+rho) prescribe a desired H-invariant coinvariant jet at nu+rho and zero jets at the other orbit points. Polynomial CRT and the explicit p=(1/|H|)sum_{w in W}q(w^-1 X) produce a W-invariant polynomial with that jet; exactly |H| equal jets survive. Thus shifted HC is onto the closed C^H fiber, and finite-module Nakayama gives surjectivity onto the entire deformed order. Kernels agree by the actual tuple action. Translation out of the facet sends each singular generic branch to its regular coset branches and therefore induces the invariant-order inclusion; its projective identification follows from the norm-comparison standard counts, once-each flag and local lift uniqueness. No generic-only dimension inference, unproved Luna slice theorem or imported universal g-finite theorem is used.

items.title: The endomorphisms of the antidominant projective form the coinvariant algebra
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be finite-dimensional complex semisimple, $\lambda$ the dominant regular integral representative of a block and $\mathcal O_\lambda$ its block with antidominant weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$. Let $C$ be the coinvariant algebra of [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]] for the Cartan reflection representation, with its grading fixed there. Then: (1) the natural maps $Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to C$ (Harish-Chandra isomorphism, shifted by $\lambda+\rho$ in the published $\operatorname{HC}_\rho$ convention, followed by the quotient map $\rho$) and $Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ (multiplication) are surjective with the same kernel; (2) consequently the multiplication map induces a canonical algebra isomorphism $$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)\ \cong\ C,$$ identifying $C$ with the endomorphism ring of the antidominant projective, canonically and independently of the choice of projective cover inside its isomorphism class; (3) the grading on the right-hand side is the internal grading of the coinvariant algebra; no graded lift of category $\mathcal O$ is asserted or used. This is Soergel's Endomorphismensatz [Soe90, Theorem 7], in the regular integral case; the companion general form for singular blocks replaces $C$ by the invariants $C^{W_\lambda}$.
items.strategy: Apply the deformed central-action lemma with $R=S_{(0)}$ and specialize its right $R$ factor at $0$. Hom base change identifies the specialization with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$, while $(R\otimes_{R^W}R)\otimes_R\mathbb C=R/(R^W_+R)\cong C$; localization does not change this finite-dimensional quotient. The action of $Z$ specializes to the shifted Harish-Chandra quotient map. Thus the two maps are surjective with the same kernel. For singular dominant integral $\lambda$, the same specialization of $R^{W_\lambda}\otimes_{R^W}R$ gives $C^{W_\lambda}$. The proof depends on the full integral deformed central-action theorem; neither a generic dimension count nor citation of the Endomorphismensatz itself supplies it.

items.title: Soergel's Struktursatz: the functor V is fully faithful on projectives
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal O_\lambda$ be a regular integral block with antidominant projective $P=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ and Soergel functor $V=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,-)$, and let $C$ be the coinvariant algebra, identified with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ by [[thm-endomorphisms-of-the-antidominant-projective-are-the-coinvariant-algebra]], so that $V$ takes values in $C$-modules. Then for every $M\in\mathcal O_\lambda$ and every projective $Q\in\mathcal O_\lambda$ the canonical map $$V\colon \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_\lambda}(M,Q)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{C\text{-mod}}(VM,VQ)$$ is an isomorphism. In particular $V$ is fully faithful on the full subcategory of projective objects of the block, and it is faithful on all of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ after passing to the quotient by the Serre subcategory of objects killed by $V$.
items.strategy: Use the complete ordinary argument in the owner dictionary note. P is the indecomposable projective-injective with antidominant essential socle; every projective-injective is a sum of P, since a simple embedded in a Verma must be the antidominant simple and this property passes through flags. The proved coinvariant top pairing makes C a Frobenius algebra, hence injective as its own module. For simple M the canonical Hom(M,P)->Hom_C(VM,C) is zero off the antidominant label and a nonzero one-dimensional map on it; both functors are exact, so finite composition-series induction gives the isomorphism for every M. Maximal-weight peeling puts Delta_dominant in P with Verma-filtered quotient. It is exactly the C_+-annihilated part: if that part were larger, its quotient would contain the antidominant simple, giving dimension>=2 under exact V, but its image in VP=C lies in the one-dimensional socle. Taking annihilated Hom subspaces gives Hom(M,Delta_dominant)=Hom_C(VM,VDelta_dominant). For a word F of wall functors, the exact adjoint word G sends P to sums of P, hence both preserve ker V. The exact quotient by ker V is C-mod: the left adjoint P tensor_C - has V of it equal to the identity, and the counit's kernel/cokernel are killed by V. The adjunction descends, so Hom(M,FDelta)=Hom(GM,Delta)=Hom_C(VGM,VDelta)=Hom_C(VM,VFDelta). Ordinary wall-word object generation supplies every projective as a summand, proving the assertion and quotient-faithfulness clause. This uses object generation, not an unnecessary functor-classification prerequisite or an unproved quotient-adjunction lemma.

items.title: Wall-crossing under the Soergel functor is tensoring with the coinvariant bimodule
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a regular integral block and simple reflection $s$, with $C=\operatorname{End}(P(w_0\cdot\lambda))$, there is a natural isomorphism of functors to left $C$-modules $$V\theta_s\cong C\otimes_{C^s}V.$$ Equivalently the functor is tensoring by the $(C,C)$-bimodule $C\otimes_{C^s}C$, with left action on the first factor and right action on the second. In type A over $\mathbb C$, its polynomial lift is tensoring on the left by $B_s=S\otimes_{S^s}S(1)$; for a right-reduced polynomial bimodule $\bar M=M\otimes_S\mathbb C$, one has $\overline{B_s\otimes_SM}\cong B_s\otimes_S\bar M\cong(C\otimes_{C^s}C)(1)\otimes_C\bar M$. Forgetting the grading gives the displayed category-$\mathcal O$ formula. The normalized self-dual rank-one reduction has generator degrees $-1,1$; shifting it to degrees $0,2$ is an alternative uncentered normalization. No grading on arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects is asserted. In particular $B_s\otimes_S\mathbb C$ itself is not the bimodule $C\otimes_{C^s}C$: the former has vector-space dimension two, whereas the latter has dimension $2|W|$.
items.strategy: The complete ordinary/deformed translation argument is in the owner dictionary note. Let H={1,s}. Dominant norm-distance and finite-dimensional extremal-weight bounds give one retained standard onto the facet and two out. Out translation sends the singular antidominant projective to the regular one, since its flag has every regular standard once and adjunction gives its antidominant cover quotient; over R local lift uniqueness proves the same identification. Its End map is the inclusion of invariant orders, checked on generic constituents. Onto translation of the regular antidominant projective is two copies of the singular one: ordinarily it is projective-injective, hence a sum of that projective, and its flag counts give two; over R local projective uniqueness lifts this, without claiming R-injectivity. Therefore V_singular T_on=Res V_regular by adjunction, and both translations preserve the V-killed subcategories. The explicit quotient equivalence from P tensor_A - and its counit descends the biadjunction; extension of scalars is adjoint to restriction, so V_regular T_out=Ind V_singular. Compose to get C tensor_{C^s}V, or the corresponding deformed R tensor_{R^s} action. The image of S^s in C is C^s by averaging representatives. Tensor reduction and the rank-two free S/S^s basis identify the polynomial B_s action, with the chosen shift; its two-dimensional right origin reduction is distinct from the 2|W|-dimensional coinvariant bimodule.

items.title: Indecomposable projectives correspond to indecomposable Soergel modules
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and work in a regular integral type-A block over $\mathbb C$. With the page's right wall-crossing convention and left $C$-module values of $V$, there is an equivalence $$V\colon\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal O_\lambda)\xrightarrow{\sim}\{\text{ungraded Soergel modules }B\otimes_S\mathbb C\},\qquad P(w\cdot\lambda)\longmapsto\bar B_{w^{-1}}.$$ The target is the additive category of direct summands of the right reductions of polynomial Bott-Samelson bimodules, or equivalently of iterated $C\otimes_{C^s}(-)$ applied to the trivial module $\mathbb C$, not to the regular module $C$. For $w=s_1\cdots s_k$, the projective is the unique new top-label summand of $\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}\Delta(\lambda)$; applying $V$ gives the new summand of $\overline{B_{s_k}\cdots B_{s_1}}$, thus the inverse label. These normalized indecomposable polynomial lifts supply self-dual auxiliary gradings; in rank one the centered degrees are $-1,1$, with degrees $0,2$ after an uncentered shift. Forgetting grading recovers the projective dictionary. More generally the ungraded equivalence with Weyl-group Soergel modules holds for every complex semisimple regular integral block; the type-A diagrammatic label comparison applies only in type A.
items.strategy: The full local reduction proof is in the owner dictionary note. First prove deformed V full faithfulness on projectives by height-one intersection. In a root DVR the two projectives are upper Verma P_a and pair projective P_b. Their mixed Hom modules have rank one; choose inclusion i and a lift j of the primitive residual map to the upper Verma. The nonzero nilpotent ij and identity form an End(P_b) basis by Nakayama. In the proved congruence order ij=(h,0), so h is a unit times alpha; rescale to ji=alpha. V sends the four Hom modules to precisely the Hom modules between the congruence order and its upper rank-one branch, with i mapping to (alpha,0) and j to projection. At nonroot primes the calculation is one-label Morita. Ordinary projective Hom is finite free over R, and A-module Hom of the finite free V-values is the intersection of its localizations by its finite generator equations; equality at all height-one primes proves full faithfulness over R. Polynomial Bott-Samelson bimodules localized on the right at0 carry the deformed central-order action and are V_R of the translated projective words. Their left denominators nonzero at0 invert on the finite right-free module by Nakayama; invariant left/right actions agree. Finite presentation of polynomial bimodule Hom and flat localization give Hom_A equal to localized polynomial Hom. Deformed full faithfulness, projective Hom base change to0, and ordinary Struktursatz consequently prove the natural reduction-of-Hom isomorphism for Bott-Samelson objects and their summands. This supplies the local proof of Garnier's reduction theorem. For complex extension, the rational polynomial degree-zero End algebra is local with residue Q; its nilpotent radical extends to a nilpotent ideal with quotient C, so remains local. The reduced degree-zero End is a quotient and local. Its finite full Z-graded End is local too: its Jacobson radical is graded by scaling/Vandermonde projections; the semisimple quotient is a product of matrices. The grading derivation on each matrix algebra is inner (c=sum D(E_i1)E_1i gives [c,E_ab]=D(E_ab)); diagonalizability of the derivation makes its degree-zero centralizer semisimple. It is also a quotient of a local algebra, hence C, forcing the whole semisimple quotient to be C. Thus reductions are indecomposable after forgetting grading. Induct on Bruhat length. For the reversed reduced word of w, every proper subexpression has label y<w; its polynomial indecomposable summands B_y, and the projective summands P_{y^-1}, have already been matched by induction. The polynomial B_w occurs once and its reduction is indecomposable; the projective P_{w^-1} occurs once by the object-generation lemma. All remaining projective summands have smaller labels. Finite Krull-Schmidt uniqueness matches the two remaining new summands, and full faithfulness ensures distinct projective labels never become isomorphic. Composition on standards follows right multiplication, while polynomial tensors act on the left, giving the inverse label w^-1. The actual invariant-intersection-form supplier supplies a nondegenerate centered reduced invariant form on each real B_w, not merely a polynomial self-duality assertion. This form descends to the rational reduction: its invariance equations are finite rational linear equations; their rational solution space extends to the real one, and the determinant polynomial is not identically zero, so over the infinite field Q a nondegenerate rational solution exists. Extending that solution to C preserves its determinant and identifies the centered reduction with its graded dual. These normalized lifts therefore supply the claimed auxiliary self-dual grading. For the permutation realization S=Q[x_1,...,x_n], split off the W-fixed average coordinate from the sl_n Cartan; it acts identically on both sides, and polynomial extension/right reduction kills it, so it changes neither the modules nor the Hom comparison. Products of type-A factors follow by tensoring the same finite projective-generator construction. No full Ext grading on O is asserted. Any two finite graded lifts with the same indecomposable underlying C-module differ by a shift: decompose an ungraded isomorphism f and its inverse g into finitely many homogeneous components. The degree-zero identity is sum_d g_{-d}f_d. Since the degree-zero End algebra is local, some g_{-d}f_d is a unit. That f_d is a split graded injection, and ungraded indecomposability of the target forces it to be a graded isomorphism after shift. For finite support, a nonzero shift of a centered self-dual module cannot remain centered self-dual, by the symmetry of its extreme degrees; thus the centered normalization is unique.

items.title: Verma-flag multiplicities are standard-filtration ranks under V
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a projective $P$ in a regular integral type-A block, choose its polynomial Soergel lift $\mathsf B(P)$ determined by the preceding projective dictionary: if $P=\bigoplus_wP(w\cdot\lambda)^{m_w}$, take $\mathsf B(P)=\bigoplus_w B_{w^{-1}}^{m_w}$, so that its right reduction is $V(P)$ after forgetting auxiliary grading. Write $r_{x,d}(\mathsf B(P))$ for the graded multiplicity of the polynomial standard graph module supported at $x$ in its standard support filtration, with the standard-generator normalization of the polynomial Soergel category. Then $$ (P:\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=\sum_d r_{y^{-1},d}(\mathsf B(P)). $$ Equivalently the polynomial Soergel character of this lift, evaluated at $v=1$ and with inverse labels, recovers the ordinary Verma-flag character of $P$. These are ranks before reduction; no separated Bruhat-support filtration intrinsic to the finite-dimensional module $V(P)$ is asserted, since the graph supports coalesce at the origin. The same ungraded multiplicity comparison holds with the corresponding Weyl-group polynomial/deformed lifts in other complex semisimple types.
items.strategy: The exact individual-rank proof is in the owner dictionary note. Deform the projective using the constructive local projective theorem and its flag/Hom base change. V_R is exact and sends each standard Delta_R(y dot lambda) to a finite free R-module of rank one, since the closed Hom dimension is [Delta_y:L_antidominant]=1, already proved by the once-each antidominant flag and BGG. Central action on that standard is f->f(y^-1 tau). In the published polynomial graph convention R_x has left coordinate x times the right parameter, so this is the graph label x=y^-1. Deformed wall crossing and the proved reduced-Hom/indecomposable dictionary identify the right-localized chosen polynomial lift B(P) with V_R P_R. After passage to the fraction field, its x-graph ranks are therefore exactly the Verma multiplicities at y=x^-1. Flat localization preserves polynomial support ranks; summing their graded multiplicities gives those ordinary ranks. The deformed flag specializes exactly, yielding the displayed comparison for every individual y at v=1. Right origin reduction supplies V(P) but collapses all graph supports, so no intrinsic labelled reduced filtration is used. The fixed permutation-realization coordinate is split off as in the preceding dictionary.
