items.title: The coinvariant algebra of S_2 and S_3 as graded regular representations
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items used. For $W=S_2$ acting on $\mathfrak h$ of dimension one: $C=\mathbb k[x]/(x^2)$, of Hilbert series $1+t^2$ in the page normalization $\deg x=2$ (equivalently $1+t$ for $\deg x=1$), with $C_0$ the trivial and $C_2$ the sign representation, so $C$ is the regular representation of $S_2$ with graded multiplicities one and one. For $W=S_3$ acting on the two-dimensional reflection representation: $C=\mathbb k[x_1,x_2,x_3]/(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ has Hilbert series $(1+t^2)(1+t^2+t^4)=1+2t^2+2t^4+t^6$ in the same normalization (equivalently $(1+t)(1+t+t^2)$ for $\deg x_i=1$) and decomposes as $C_0=$ trivial, $C_2=$ standard, $C_4=$ standard$\otimes$sign, $C_6=$ sign, the graded lift of the regular representation with graded multiplicities $1$ for the trivial module, $t^6$ for the sign module and $t^2+t^4$ for the two-dimensional standard module. In both cases the graded character identity of [[thm-the-weyl-coinvariant-algebra-is-the-graded-regular-representation]] evaluates to the regular representation's character and the sum of the graded multiplicities times dimensions recovers $|W|$.
items.strategy: Direct computation of the quotient by the basic invariants in the given coordinates; the Hilbert series is [[lem-weyl-coinvariant-hilbert-series-has-order-w-dimension]] with the basic degrees $1,2$ (respectively $1,2,3$); the identification of the graded pieces with the named $S_n$-modules is by comparing characters at the transpositions and the three-cycle, and the conclusion is the general theorem. The example is a verification of the general statement in the smallest cases and is not used as evidence for it.

items.title: The wall-crossing functor on Verma modules in rank one
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. In $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ let $\lambda=0$, $\rho=1$, regular standards $\Delta_1=M(0)$, $\Delta_s=M(-2)$, and singular wall weight $\mu=-1$, whose shifted weight $\mu+\rho=0$. The translating finite-dimensional simple has highest weight1 and dimension2. Translation onto the wall sends both regular standards to $M(-1)$; translation out gives the projective $P(-2)$. Thus both $\theta_s\Delta_1$ and $\theta_s\Delta_s$ have the same nonsplit standard extension $$0\to M(0)\to P(-2)\to M(-2)\to0,$$ and their classes are $[\Delta_1]+[\Delta_s]$. The wall is -1 in highest-weight coordinates, or0 in shifted coordinates.
items.strategy: Apply the extremal-weight tensor filtration to the natural two-dimensional module and project to the indicated central character. There is one retained wall standard and two retained return standards. The return is projective because M(-1) is the projective simple in its one-simple block and return translation is exact biadjoint. Its once-each flag and antidominant simple quotient identify it with P(-2). Maximal-weight peeling puts M(0) first; nonsplitting follows from indecomposability of that cover. The zero wall is the shifted parameter mu+rho, not the regular highest weight0.

items.title: The class map and the wall-crossing action in rank two
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items used. In type $A_2$ with simple reflections $s,t$ of order three, the classes of the standards in the regular integral block are $[\Delta_1],[\Delta_s],[\Delta_t],[\Delta_{st}],[\Delta_{ts}],[\Delta_{sts}]$, and the class map sends them to the elements of $W=S_3$; the wall-crossing functors act by right multiplication by $1+s$ and $1+t$, so that $$[\theta_s\theta_t\Delta_1]=[\Delta_1]+[\Delta_t]+[\Delta_s]+[\Delta_{ts}]$$ while $$[\theta_t\theta_s\Delta_1]=[\Delta_1]+[\Delta_s]+[\Delta_t]+[\Delta_{st}],$$ exhibiting the non-commutativity of the wall-crossing action and matching the multiplication of the corresponding standard generators in the Hecke algebra of $S_3$. The example also computes the standard multiplicities of the projective $\theta_s\theta_t\Delta_1$: by the unitriangularity of BGG reciprocity the indecomposable summand $P(ts\cdot\lambda)$ occurs with multiplicity one and the remaining summands have smaller labels.
items.strategy: Read off the class formula from [[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-the-grothendieck-group-by-right-multiplication-by-one-plus-s]] applied first to $\Delta_1$ and then to the two-factor objects; the two computations differ in the label of the length-two factor ($ts$ versus $st$), which are distinct elements of $S_3$ and hence distinct Verma classes by the standard basis theorem [[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]]. The projective multiplicities follow from [[lem-wall-crossing-compositions-produce-the-projective-with-the-top-standard-label]] for the word ts (since theta_s theta_t applies t first), with the corrected standard-support triangle y<=x of the Verma-flag matrix.

items.title: Wall-crossing functors do not commute
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items used. In type $A_2$ with distinct simple reflections $s,t$, the projective functors $\theta_s\theta_t$ and $\theta_t\theta_s$ on the regular integral block are not naturally equivalent: on the standard object $\Delta(\lambda)$ their classes are $[\Delta(\lambda)]+[\Delta(t\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(s\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ts\cdot\lambda)]$ and $[\Delta(\lambda)]+[\Delta(s\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(t\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(st\cdot\lambda)]$, which differ because $st\neq ts$ and the Verma classes are linearly independent. So the wall-crossing functors do not define a representation of $W$; they categorify the Hecke algebra of $W$, in which $H_sH_t\neq H_tH_s$ for $m_{st}=3$, rather than the group algebra. The counterexample is the functor-level sharpening of the rank-two class computation and shows that 'generated by wall-crossing' cannot be read as 'representation of $W$'.
items.strategy: Compute both classes with [[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-the-grothendieck-group-by-right-multiplication-by-one-plus-s]], using that the Verma classes are a basis ([[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]] and the standard-basis theorem for the Grothendieck group); the labels $st$ and $ts$ are distinct elements of $S_3$, and the two induced operators on the standard generators differ, so the induced operators on $K_0$ differ. By the determination theorem [[thm-indecomposable-projective-functors-are-indexed-by-the-weyl-group]](3) a difference on the Grothendieck group implies that the functors are not naturally equivalent; the standard objects generate the Grothendieck group, so it suffices to evaluate on the single object $\Delta(\lambda)$. No claim is made about the existence of a nontrivial natural transformation; the obstruction is already the class.

items.title: Wall-crossing on the projectives in the sl_2 block
items.statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. In the regular integral sl_2 block with lambda=0, rho=1, s dot 0=-2 and singular wall weight mu=-1, the indecomposable projectives are P_e=M(0) and P_s=P(-2). The wall-crossing functor theta_s satisfies theta_s(P_e)≅P_s and theta_s(P_s)≅P_s⊕P_s. In ordered projective bases (P_e,P_s), its matrix, with columns as inputs, is ((0,0),(1,2)). On the Soergel side C=k[x]/(x²), C^s=k and V(P_e)=k, V(P_s)=C; hence V theta_s(P_e)=C⊗_k k≅C and V theta_s(P_s)=C⊗_k C≅C⊕C as left C-modules. The latter tensor is the four-dimensional coinvariant bimodule (left C acts on the first factor), while the right-reduced polynomial B_s is only two dimensional. The result computes wall-crossing on projective objects, in addition to the preserved existing computation on Verma modules.
items.strategy: For the first equality, apply the existing projective-generation and two-step wall-extension lemmas to the one-letter reduced word: theta_s M(0)=P(-2), with standard flag M(0),M(-2). For the second equality, exact biadjoint translation preserves projectives. Apply theta_s to the flag 0→M(0)→P_s→M(-2)→0. Its two outer values are P_s by the existing rank-one two-step extension, so theta_s P_s has standard multiplicities (2,2). Every projective in this two-simple block is a sum of P_e and P_s, whose flags have multiplicities (1,0),(1,1) by BGG reciprocity. The equations a+b=2 and b=2 give a=0,b=2, proving the object isomorphism without treating a class identity as an isomorphism by itself. Alternatively compute with the existing wall-crossing-under-V theorem: s(x)=-x gives C^s=k; the left C-linear isomorphism C⊕C→C⊗_k C sends (u,v) to u⊗1+v⊗x. The projective Struktursatz reflects this isomorphism because all objects concerned are projective. Display both tensor basis and projective multiplicity calculation; no generated B item is a dependency.

items.title: The Soergel functor on the small regular sl_2 block
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the category-O suppliers. Work over k=C in the dominant regular integral sl_2 block at lambda=0, with rho=1 and W={e,s}, so s dot 0=-2. Put Delta_e=M(0), Delta_s=M(-2)=L(-2), P_e=P(0)=Delta_e and P_s=P(-2). There are nonsplit sequences 0→L(-2)→Delta_e→L(0)→0 and 0→Delta_e→P_s→Delta_s→0. With C=k[x]/(x²), deg x=2, and V=Hom(P_s,-), the left C-module values are V(P_e)=k=C/(x), V(P_s)=C, V(Delta_e)=V(Delta_s)=k, V(L(0))=0 and V(L(-2))=k. The projective Hom table, with rows as sources P_e,P_s and columns as targets P_e,P_s, is ((k,k),(k,C)); thus the four dimensions are ((1,1),(1,2)). Choose i:k→C, i(1)=x, and p:C→k, p(a+bx)=a. Under the Struktursatz these are the nonzero mixed projective maps, with p i=0 and i p=m_x, multiplication by x. This explicitly computes End(P_s)=C and the projective full-faithfulness comparison, rather than claiming full faithfulness on the whole block. For S=k[a], s(a)=-a, the polynomial lifts B_e=S and B_s=S⊗_{k[a²]}S(1) reduce on the right to k and C(1); their labels are e^{-1}=e and s^{-1}=s. The centered auxiliary degrees on C(1) are -1,1. Before reduction the standard graph ranks (e,s) are (1,0) for B_e and (1,1) for B_s, agreeing with the Verma-flag multiplicities of P_e and P_s at v=1. These ranks are taken before graph supports coalesce at the origin; no grading on arbitrary O objects or intrinsic separated-support filtration on V(P) is asserted.
items.strategy: Use only the named current A-page suppliers and explicit rank-one algebra. In the PBW basis f^n v of M(t), e f^n v=n(t-n+1)f^{n-1}v. At t=0, f v is a singular vector generating M(-2), and the quotient is the one-dimensional L(0); at t=-2 every n>0 coefficient is nonzero, proving simplicity. Highest-weight generation gives nonsplitting of the first sequence. The empty-word case of the projective-generation lemma makes Delta_e=P_e; its one-wall case and the two-step extension lemma give the second sequence and P_s. Since Hom(P_s,L_y) is k for its head y=s and zero for y=e, exactness of V and the displayed composition factors give dimensions 1,2,1,1,0,1 in the stated order. Endomorphismensatz identifies V(P_s) with the regular C-module. The only one-dimensional C-module has x acting by zero, identifying every nonzero dimension-one value with k. Compute Hom_C(k,k)=k, Hom_C(k,C)=kx (annihilator of x), Hom_C(C,k)=k and Hom_C(C,C)=C. Struktursatz with projective targets identifies the four actual O-Hom spaces and compositions; normalize i,p so i(1)=x and p(1)=1, then pi=0 and ip=m_x on the basis 1,x. Independently, the polynomial model for B_s is k[l,r]/(l²-r²)(1). Right reduction r=0 gives k[l]/l²(1). The submodule (l-r) is free rank one on graph l=-r and the quotient is free rank one on graph l=r; the annihilator of l-r is (l+r), since cancellation in k[l,r] is valid. Thus its two standard graph layers have ranks one each. The e lift has only the e graph. Compare the two once-each/one-only Verma flags, invoking the existing multiplicity supplier with total ranks only. The fixed average coordinate in the published two-variable permutation realization is split off and killed on reduction, as explicitly allowed by the existing A-page dictionary. These finite computations illustrate those suppliers, rather than proving their general claims.

items.title: The Soergel functor is not fully faithful on all category-O objects
items.statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. The assertion that V=Hom(P(-2),-) is fully faithful on every object of the regular integral sl_2 block at lambda=0 is false. Let L_0=L(0) be the nonzero one-dimensional simple. Then V(L_0)=0 and the nonzero identity in Hom_O(L_0,L_0)=k maps to zero in Hom_C(0,0)=0: V is not faithful. It also fails fullness on Hom_O(M(0),L(-2)): that Hom space is zero, whereas V(M(0))=V(L(-2))=k=C/(x) and Hom_C(k,k)=k. Both counterexamples have a nonprojective target, so they do not contradict the Struktursatz, which requires its target Q to be projective (and allows an arbitrary source). Passing to the quotient by the V-killed Serre subcategory is a separate assertion and is not refuted.
items.strategy: Compute directly, without relying on another generated B example as a supplier. In the PBW basis, e f^n v=n(t-n+1)f^{n-1}v shows the nonsplit 0→L(-2)→M(0)→L(0)→0 and simplicity of M(-2)=L(-2). P(-2) has unique simple head L(-2), so its Hom to L(0) is zero and its Hom to L(-2) is one dimensional. Exactness of Hom(P(-2),-) then gives V(M(0)) one dimensional; x²=0 makes x act zero on both one-dimensional values. A homomorphism M(0)→L(-2) must send its cyclic highest-weight vector of weight0 to a weight0 vector. The weights of L(-2) are -2,-4,..., so no such vector exists and the Hom is zero. Thus the induced zero→k map is not onto. End(L(0))=k follows directly from its one-dimensional underlying space, giving the independent failure of faithfulness. L(0) is nonprojective since the first nonsplit epimorphism onto it would otherwise split. L(-2) is nonprojective since the nonsplit 0→M(0)→P(-2)→L(-2)→0 from the existing two-step wall extension would otherwise split. State the target-projective hypothesis explicitly; do not replace it by the weaker both-projective wording.
